ideas.description: Exploit: a time-neutral test that separates the two parts of the freeze-dose cost. On the E061 tip (225 steps), change only the end point of the group-1 LR anneal (conv filters on Muon; BN params on SGD): it moves from 75% to 80% of steps, so group 1's LR decays more slowly over the whole run. The group-1 detach stays at 75% (same absolute step), so the frozen variant covers exactly the same steps and time is unchanged. At the detach, the group-1 LR is then about 5/57 ≈ 9% of peak instead of 0. E009 and C0021 say the LR floor does not matter under Lookahead averaging. Whitening detach, group-2 freeze, resolution, step count, Lookahead and LS are unchanged. If the LR is a GPU tensor table, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (60 draws) against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. This is the time-neutral form of H2.6.13. E055's −0.29 pp moved the anneal end and the detach together; this moves only the anneal.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.02 s). If decay compression drives E055's cost, the 60-draw mean rises +0.05 to +0.15 pp (median +0.07). That is a free booster and would raise the local pass probability from ~50% to ~65%. A change within ±0.03 pp means the cost of earlier freezes comes from lost late steps; the freeze point itself (H2.6.12) is then the lever. A loss ≥0.1 pp means group 1 needs to reach LR 0 before the detach.

ideas.description: Exploit, a margin buyer priced against the dial. On the E061 tip, move the group-1 detach and its LR anneal end together from 75% to 80% of steps (~11 more unfrozen 32 px steps at ~7.7 ms each, ≈ +0.09 s). Step count (225), whitening detach (6%), group-2 freeze (75→90% anneal, detach at 90%), resolution, LR triangle, Lookahead and LS are unchanged. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Record per-step CUDA-event time. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Rationale: E055 shows a steep dose (−0.29 pp for freezing 4% earlier). E028's 'free' reading at 75% was a 10-seed result with SE ~0.12 pp, so the slope may continue past 75%. Run after the anneal-only idea, if possible, so its result can be split into anneal and step components.
ideas.expected: Time +0.07 to +0.10 s (~+1.8%, to ~5.10 s). 60-draw mean +0.05 to +0.25 pp (median +0.12). Break-even at 0.77 s/pp is ~0.12 pp. A gain ≥0.15 pp beats the dial and should be spent on the early trim (I099), for a net time cut at higher margin. A gain ≤0.05 pp confirms that 75% sits on the flat side of the knee, so the freeze point is settled.

ideas.description: Exploit, a time-neutral optimizer booster on the axis H8 says is load-bearing. On the E061 tip, raise the Muon lr for every conv-filter group from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5). The per-group schedules (group-1 anneal to 75%, group-2 anneal 75→90%), momentum 0.6, wd ×0.5, the SGD groups, batch, step count, resolution, freezes, Lookahead and LS are all unchanged. If the lr is baked into the graph, recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws (SE of the difference ~0.06 pp), then the frozen gate. E014 read +0.09 pp at 3 seeds on the higher-wd base. E062 shows that per-step update quality dominates at ~225 steps, and the CIFAR-10 airbench94 lr was never retuned for this regime.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 60-draw mean −0.10 to +0.20 pp (median +0.06). A gain ≥0.12 pp supports H1.5.6 and H8.1, and funds ~0.1 s of trimming. The next point is then ×2 or a momentum retune. A loss ≥0.1 pp puts the optimum at ≤0.24 and closes the upward lr direction.

ideas.description: Exploit, a systems change with identical math, gated on a measurement (crux of W3/W5). Step 1, offline on E061 code with synthetic batch-2000 data: put CUDA events around the optimizer section of each step variant (Muon momentum + NS + update for the 3 filter groups, SGD groups, Lookahead). Record the GPU time and the host wall gap per step, and count the kernels and DtoD memcpys per step (E076 found ~51/step from mutated-input write-backs). Step 2 runs only if the non-NS optimizer overhead × 225 steps projects ≥0.05 s. Then replace the per-group Muon calls with one compiled function that does a foreach Nesterov momentum update over all filter tensors and NS with batched bmm over shape-identical filters (g1.conv2/3, g2.conv2/3, g3.conv2/3 each stack to one bmm; singletons run alone). Per-group LRs are read from one GPU-resident [groups × steps] table indexed by a GPU step counter, so there are no Python scalars and no write-back copies. Frozen groups are excluded through static per-variant parameter lists. Check offline that the updates match the current code to bf16 tolerance over 20 steps. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge time on per-step CUDA events plus 2 builds' wall time, and accuracy on 2 builds × seeds 33–52 (must sit within 0.08 pp of E061), then the frozen gate.
ideas.expected: Step 1: optimizer overhead beyond NS is ~0.2–0.5 ms/step (median), i.e. 0.05–0.1 s/trial. If it qualifies: time −1 to −2% (to ~4.93–4.97 s); accuracy within rebuild noise (±0.05 pp on 40 draws). If Step 1 shows the 0.28 s E062 gap is fully explained by NS + SGD-vs-Muon GPU time, close H2.2.5 (refuted) with no run.

ideas.description: Explore, a decisive test of the Muon-momentum crux. On the E061 tip, change only the Muon momentum for every conv-filter group from 0.6 to 0.8 (Nesterov kept; lr, wd, per-group schedules, batch, step count, freezes, Lookahead and LS unchanged). If the momentum is a baked constant, recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Two accounts disagree. Muon critical-batch theory (b* falls at higher β, with batch 2000 already large) and the CIFAR-100 critical-damping result predict harm. H8.1 predicts that more momentum smooths per-step noise in a 225-step run with heavy LS and Lookahead resets, and gains. The 0.6 value comes from CIFAR-10 airbench94 and has never been varied here.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 60-draw mean −0.30 to +0.15 pp (median −0.05). A gain ≥0.12 pp supports H8.1.1: then test 0.7 combined with any lr gain. A loss ≥0.12 pp refutes it and points the next probe at 0.5 (the critical-batch direction).

ideas.description: Explore diagnostic, offline, outside submissions/arena/, with no recipe change. It routes the remaining booster search. Run an instrumented copy of the E061 tip on real training data for seeds 33–35. After train() returns, evaluate the final averaged weights (eval mode, as in the submission) on a fixed 10k subset of the 50k training images at 32 px with no augmentation. Record top-1 and plain CE (no LS). For contrast, also record the same metrics for the fast weights just before the final Lookahead copy, and train top-1 on the last 32 px epoch's augmented batches (logged during training). Never touch the test set beyond the harness's normal eval. Write the numbers to the notebook.
ideas.expected: Task metrics unchanged (E061: ~5.02 s, ~0.753). Predicted clean train top-1 is 85–93% (median ~89%), i.e. under-fitting, and the averaged weights read 1–3 pp above the fast weights. If ≤90%: regularizer additions (LS ↓, jitter, ghost BN) stay deprioritized and optimizer/freeze-later boosters lead. If ≥97%: the recipe is fitting-saturated, so queue LS 0.15 (H1.5.5) and jitter (H1.5.8) on 60 draws and deprioritize Muon retuning.

drop.reason: All 4 members forecast no improvement (0/4 improve votes): the group-3 width cut is expected at about the dial's rate or worse (E010 precedent ~1.4 s/pp on 100 classes, with late capacity still binding). A cut at the dial rate cannot buy the ~0.13 pp of local margin the binding H4 constraint needs, so it is dominated by the time-neutral boosters now queued.

The committee forecasts it flat (1/4 improve, conflict 0), and whether reduced LS can help depends on whether the recipe under-fits. The new H8.2.1 diagnostic decides that at almost no cost. LS 0.15 is re-queued only if the diagnostic shows fitting saturation (train top-1 ≥97%).

structured_output.summary: The tip is E061: 5.02 s, with a population mean of about 0.7532, so it passes the local 0.753 bar only about half the time per build. The binding constraint is buying about 0.13 pp of margin with near-time-neutral boosters, and then spending any surplus on early trims. Queue after this round: I099 (the early-trim dose; it crashed as E063 on a warm-up bug that has since been fixed, so it should simply be relaunched), I097 (the gated tanh-GELU/SiLU check, kept because it settles the W3 vs W5 crux at the cost of one offline profile) and six new ideas. Exploit: (1) a time-neutral group-1 anneal extension (anneal end 75%→80%, detach kept at 75%), which separates decay compression from lost late steps in E055's cost (H2.6.13); (2) freeze plus anneal moved to 80% for +0.09 s, where break-even is about 0.12 pp at the dial (H2.6.12); (3) Muon lr ×1.5 on 60 draws (H1.5.6); (4) a measurement-gated merge of the per-group Muon calls into one compiled, batched update, with identical math (H2.2.5, the W3/W5 crux on E062's unexplained ~0.1 s). Explore: (5) Muon momentum 0.6→0.8 as the decisive test between critical-batch theory and H8.1 (H8.1.1); (6) an offline under-fitting diagnostic that decides whether regularizer boosters such as LS ↓ or jitter are worth any further runs (H8.2.1). Dropped: I100, where the group-3 width cut is forecast at about the dial rate (0/4 improve) and so cannot buy margin, and I103, the LS 0.15 test forecast flat, now gated on the H8.2.1 diagnostic. If both freeze-timing ideas and the lr booster win, stack them and spend the gain on I099's trim.
